symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on upper leaf surface
Deformed, cracked, or corky lesions on fruit skin
Premature leaf drop and stunted fruit growth
organic_remedies: Spray liquid copper soap or neem oil at early bud break
Apply bio-fungicide containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens
Rake and burn fallen infected leaves in autumn to disrupt overwintering spores
chemical_treatments: Apply Myclobutanil or Captan preventive fungicide at pink-bud stage
Rotate with Difenoconazole to prevent fungal resistance development
preventive_protocols: Prune canopy tree branches to maximize sunlight penetration and air circulation

symptoms: Frog-eye leaf spots with dark purple margins and pale centers
Blackening and rotting of fruit starting from calyx end

preventive_protocols: Disinfect pruning shears with 70% isopropyl alcohol between cuts
Keep orchard trees properly fertilized and stress-free
Burn or deeply bury all pruned infected trimmings

symptoms: Bright orange-yellow circular spots on upper leaf surface
Small tube-like fruiting structures (aecia) on lower leaf surface

organic_remedies: Apply sulfur or liquid copper fungicide as leaves emerge in spring
Remove nearby wild Eastern Red Cedar junipers within a 1-mile radius

preventive_protocols: Plant rust-resistant apple varieties like Red Delicious, McIntosh, or Gala

symptoms: Vibrant green, unblemished foliage

symptoms: Deep green, glossy leaves free from spots or yellowing

Ensure consistent drip irrigation without waterlogging root zones

symptoms: Lush green, unblemished leaf blades
Vigorous spur growth and clear tree bark

symptoms: Rectangular tan-to-gray lesions restricted by leaf veins

symptoms: Cinnamon-brown to reddish oval pustules (uredinia) on upper and lower leaf surfaces

symptoms: Deep green, broad leaves free of spots or striping

symptoms: Small reddish-brown circular spots on leaves with tiny black dots (pycnidia)

symptoms: Vibrant green, fully expanded leaf blades
